comparison: Both evaluate background claims C1, C10-C14 on sepsis epidemiology and treatment challenges. OpenEval finds them supported by appropriate citations; peer reviewers accept these claims without challenge, implicitly supporting the clinical significance framing.

Both evaluate background claims C2-C3, C15-C21 on ATP as inflammatory mediator. OpenEval finds all claims supported by established literature; peer reviewers accept these as established knowledge without questioning, providing foundation for study rationale.

Both evaluate claims C22-C27 on bacterial ATP release. OpenEval finds them supported but notes small sample size (N=2) limits statistical power. Peer reviewers describe this as 'the most compelling part of the study' with no concerns about sample size, showing stronger endorsement.

Both evaluate claims C4, C28-C30, C57-C60 on Keio collection mutant analysis. OpenEval finds mechanistic interpretation reasonable though inferential; peer reviewers explicitly call this 'the most compelling part' and 'meticulously examine' the relationship, showing strong agreement with more enthusiastic endorsement.

Both evaluate claims C5, C31-C34, C61-C63 on porin mutants and membrane integrity. OpenEval finds statistical demonstration adequate and methodological comparison appropriate; peer reviewers accept the flow cytometry methodology improvement without challenge, showing full agreement.

Both evaluate in vivo sepsis claims C35-C41 (peer also includes C6, C74). OpenEval finds survival differences and immune changes statistically supported. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting difficulty correlating increased neutrophils with tissue damage hypothesis and questioning whether effects are ATP-specific or from other bacterial components. Significant disagreement on interpretation.

Both evaluate OMV characterization claims C7, C42-C46, C64-C65, C71-C72. OpenEval acknowledges artificial loading as limitation but finds evidence converging and necessary for controlled experiments. Peer reviewers accept the OMV characterization and approach without methodological concerns, showing agreement.

Both evaluate OMV biodistribution and uptake claims C8, C47-C52. OpenEval finds descriptive analyses well-documented with adequate sample sizes. Peer reviewers accept the biodistribution data without challenge, though question why lung neutrophils were used for RNAseq. Overall agreement with minor methodological question.

Both evaluate transcriptional response claims C9, C53-C56, C68-C69 (peer excludes C66-C67). OpenEval finds RNA-seq data well-documented but notes harmful effects interpretation is speculative though appropriately qualified. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating mechanistic proof is 'interesting but not definitively convincing' and noting difficulty combining OMV and E. coli infection analyses. Disagreement on strength of mechanistic conclusions.

Both evaluate claims C70, C73 on ATP release mechanisms and extrapolations. OpenEval finds C70 supported by data and C73 a reasonable extrapolation from literature. Peer reviewers also evaluate C66-C67, C74 together, accepting interpretive claims without direct challenge. Partial overlap with general agreement.

Both evaluate ethical compliance claims C75-C77. OpenEval notes these are standard methodological claims appropriately documented. Peer reviewers accept them as meeting publication requirements without question. Complete agreement.
